changes.current_line: Proven ROI, backed by an independent economic impact study.
changes.change: When the champion starts asking for payback, replace the generic study with a payback model built with the champion from their own inputs: engineering time per pricing change, billing errors, and revenue lost to subscriptions that lapse on failed cards. Make it CFO-ready and get it to finance early, not at the end. Suggested line: Your payback, in your own numbers, so your CFO sees 'a number that's ours'.
changes.why: Owen asked 'do you have something that shows payback?', got the general ROI deck with the study, and said 'I can't get this past Diane without a number that's ours', and the session to build that number never happened.

changes.current_line: Billing that helps you grow revenue.
changes.change: For buyers replacing a homegrown billing system, stop leading with revenue growth. Lead with: Change a price in a few clicks instead of spending a quarter of roadmap on it, so billing stops being 'a tax on the roadmap'. Attach what that roadmap time costs in dollars.
changes.why: The champion corrected the revenue framing outright ('we're not trying to grow revenue with billing, we're trying to stop it being a tax on the roadmap'), while the price-change demo landed as 'a quarter of roadmap in five minutes'.

changes.current_line: Recover failed payments automatically with smart retries.
changes.change: For subscription businesses where finance decides, add a proof point to this line: an estimate of the subscription revenue currently lost when cards fail and nobody chases it, calculated from the buyer's own figures, and feed it into the payback case.
changes.why: The champion mentioned that 'some landlord subscriptions lapse because the card fails and nobody chases it', but 'We never added it up', and the missing piece was 'The number. Their own.'

changes.change: For buyers moving off an existing billing system, add a migration proof point: a reference customer the buyer can talk to who moved existing subscriptions without asking customers for their card details again, and who did it in stages. Offer the call alongside the migration doc, not instead of it.
changes.why: Owen's concern was moving existing subscriptions without re-collecting card details and whether it could happen in stages, and when offered a doc 'He wanted to talk to someone who'd done it.'
